headline: Reviewing the fleet from the Mayflower
summary: From the deck of the Mayflower, Roosevelt reviews the ships of the North Atlantic Squadron with a party that includes the Dunnes, the Bacons, the Bonapartes, the La Farges and Commander Sims, and has the Dunnes and Bacons to dinner aboard.

events.detail: Dinner on the yacht with the Dunnes and Bacons

uncertain: Review location not named in source; Long Island Sound assumed for the Oyster Bay review.

headline: Hughes for governor
summary: Roosevelt writes Gardner on immigration limits, asks Vice President Fairbanks to speak in Chicago, sends Root a long letter on his tour, the naval review, the elections, Bryan and Hughes for governor, and writes Lodge about the Supreme Court choice.

letters.topic: Limits on immigration
Wants him to give a Chicago speech
His trip, the fleet review, elections, Bryan, Hughes
Deciding the Supreme Court appointment

headline: An evening at the Masonic lodge
summary: Roosevelt hears tariff reformers H. E. Miles and Lyman Bass, talks New York politics over lunch with Cortelyou and Littauer, and spends time at his Masonic lodge in town. He defends Joe Cannon to Edgar Clark and writes Florence La Farge about the Greek play Electra.

headline: The Longworths come to stay

letters.topic: Capping battleship size; the Hague Conference

headline: Bamie and Will visit
summary: Roosevelt's sister Bamie and her husband Will Cowles are guests, and he confers with A. R. Page.

headline: Two warships for Cuba
summary: Roosevelt speaks at Christ Church in Oyster Bay for its 200th anniversary and confers with Bacon and Reynolds. He wires Bonaparte to send two warships to Cuba to protect American interests, and tells James Bede that his Watson letter will be his only endorsement of Republican candidates.

headline: Balfour, Newfoundland and Cuba
summary: Roosevelt writes Sir George Otto Trevelyan about Arthur Balfour and British distrust of him, and about unrest in Cuba and the Newfoundland dispute.

headline: Lunch with Homer Saint-Gaudens

summary: On Ted's 19th birthday, Roosevelt learns that 125 Marines have gone ashore in Cuba without his authority and wires Bacon to pull them back to the ships. He writes Moody on the Washington ice trust, Standard Oil and spelling, and Harvard's President Eliot about honoring Walter Reed.

headline: Ready to send troops to Cuba
summary: Roosevelt meets Taft, Bacon and Bonaparte about the revolt in Cuba, lunches on the Mayflower and greets a yacht race delegation. He tells Bacon that if President Palma resigns he will send troops, and explains to Cuban Minister Quesada why that is necessary.

Army plans for Cuba; lock canal; western races

summary: Roosevelt writes Indian Commissioner Leupp about Flynn, Frantz and investigations in the Indian service.

Eight-hour rule applied to government work

headline: Rowing, tennis and chopping trees

Quentin hopes to join his friend Mike Landon at the Fay School, which pains Edith; Archie is sailing with Emlen; and the family went to church, where Ethel met them after Sunday school.

summary: Roosevelt proclaims Devils Tower in Wyoming the first national monument under the new Antiquities Act.
